title: ACA s. 7 — Arbitration agreement defined (ACA s. 7)

content.overview: Section 7 defines an arbitration agreement as an agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes which have arisen or which may arise between them in respect of a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not. The agreement must be in writing, including forms specified in the section such as a document signed by the parties, exchange of communications, or exchange of statements of claim and defence in which the existence of the agreement is alleged and not denied.
content.glance: Written agreement to submit disputes arising from a defined legal relationship to arbitration; writing includes the forms listed in s. 7(4).
content.study: Section 7 is the definitional core of the Act. Existence and validity of the arbitration agreement are tested at referral (ss. 8, 11) on a prima facie standard and more fully before the tribunal under s. 16. Incorporation of an arbitration clause from another document requires clear intention.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Agreement to submit to arbitration disputes arising from a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not.

sections.heading: Writing requirement
sections.body: The agreement must be in writing, including the forms in section 7(4).

sections.heading: Incorporation
sections.body: Reference to another document may incorporate an arbitration clause only if the intention to incorporate that clause is clear.

cases.name: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
cases.facts: Reference on arbitrability and the standard of review under sections 8 and 11.
cases.issue: When does a valid arbitration agreement exist for referral purposes, and when is a dispute non-arbitrable?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Four-fold test for non-arbitrability; referral courts apply a prima facie standard — when in doubt, refer; only clear cases of non-existence or non-arbitrability justify refusal.
cases.holding: Tenancy disputes under the TPA are arbitrable unless governed by a special statute; fraud is not a general bar to reference.
cases.relevance: Leading authority on section 7 existence/validity analysis at the referral stage and on subject-matter arbitrability.

cases.name: M.R. Engineers & Contractors (P) Ltd. v. Som Datt Builders Ltd.
cases.facts: Dispute on whether a general reference to another contract incorporated its arbitration clause into the subcontract.
cases.issue: When does a reference to another document incorporate an arbitration agreement under section 7?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A general reference to another contract does not automatically incorporate its arbitration clause; clear intention to incorporate the arbitration clause is required.
cases.holding: Arbitration clause was not incorporated by a mere general reference.
cases.relevance: Classic authority on incorporation of arbitration agreements under section 7.
